unit.can_do_en: introduce myself at work and ask where things are.

brief.situation_en: Maria asks Hanna about her week.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Hanna, mihin aikaan mun työpäivä alkaa?
lines.text_kirja: Hanna, mihin aikaan minun työpäiväni alkaa?
lines.gloss_en: Hanna, what time does my working day start?

judge.reason: Only register differences (mun/minun, työpäiväni possessive); same question about start time.

puhe.text: Hanna, mihin aikaan mun työpäivä alkaa?

kirja.text: Hanna, mihin aikaan minun työpäiväni alkaa?

lines.speaker: Hanna
lines.gloss_en: At eight. And it ends at four.

judge.reason: Kaheksalta is the spoken form of kahdeksalta; same times (eight, four).

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Do I work on Saturdays too?

judge.reason: Teenks mä/Teenkö minä: same question about working on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Hanna
lines.text_puhe: Et. Sä teet töitä maanantaist perjantaihin.
lines.text_kirja: Et. Sinä teet töitä maanantaista perjantaihin.
lines.gloss_en: No. You work Monday to Friday.

judge.reason: Same negation and same days, Monday to Friday; only register differs.

puhe.text: Et. Sä teet töitä maanantaist perjantaihin.

kirja.text: Et. Sinä teet töitä maanantaista perjantaihin.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Good. Can I work from home?

judge.reason: Voinks mä tehä/Voinko minä tehdä: same question about remote work.
Joo and kyllä both mean yes; perjantaisin is the same.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Nice! Where do I get a key card?

judge.reason: Mist mä/Mistä minä: same question about where to get the key card.

lines.speaker: Hanna
lines.gloss_en: From the lobby. I'll come with you.

judge.reason: Mä tuun sun kaa = Minä tulen sinun kanssasi; same meaning, 'I'll come with you'.

forms.why_en: Mikä with -hin for 'to': mihin, where to.
Aika with -an. Mihin aikaan? means at what time?
Minä with -n: minun pitää means I have to. Speech shortens it to mun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for my
forms.why_en: Books add -ni for 'my': työpäiväni. Speech drops it and says mun työpäivä.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Adds -lta for a time on the clock: kahdeksan becomes kahdeksalta. Speech drops the d: kaheksalta.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Loppua 'to end' doubles its last vowel for 'it': se loppuu. People say it the same way.
Adds -ltä for a time on the clock: neljä becomes neljältä.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 1st person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Teen (I do) with the question ending -kö: teenkö. Speech says teenks.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Työ becomes töitä after tehdä: tehdä töitä means 'to work'. The vowels change from yö to ö.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Days take -na for 'on': lauantai becomes lauantaina.
The word for 'not' changes to match the person: et is 'you don't'. A short et answers a question with no.
Speech shortens sinä to sä. Books write sinä.
Tehdä changes to tee- and takes -t for 'you': teet.
Maanantai with -sta for 'from': maanantaista. Speech drops the last vowel: maanantaist.
Perjantai with -hin for 'to': perjantaihin, as in Monday to Friday.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 1st person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Voin, I can, with -ko to ask. Speech says -ks: voinks.
This is the dictionary form, after voin (I can). Speech drops the d: tehä.
Etätyö becomes etätöitä after tehdä: tehdä etätöitä means 'to work from home'.
Joo is the everyday spoken yes. Books write kyllä.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Mikä with -stä for 'from': mistä. Speech drops the last vowel: mist.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to get, to be allowed to
forms.why_en: Saada drops -da and takes -n for 'I': saan.
Adds -n for the thing you get or receive: avainkortti becomes avainkortin, with one t.
Adds -sta for 'from': aula becomes aulasta.
Adds -en for 'I': tulla becomes tulen. Speech says tuun.
Sinä with -n for 'your': sinun. Speech shortens it to sun.

forms.form_name_en: adposition, with the possessive ending for your
forms.why_en: Books write sinun kanssasi, adding -si for 'your'. Speech says sun kaa, a short form of kanssa.
